correctness.rationale: For c != 0 and B>3c^2/4 the objective has positive definite Hessian. The cubic Taylor Hessian lower-right diagonal requires t>=3c^2/4. At equality the quadratic form in each normalized direction has minimum (1-q^2)^2(1+2q^2)>=0, proving convexity; the established bivariate quartic convexity/SOS-convexity equivalence proves feasibility. The exact invariant-axis scalar minimizer has derivative lambda-3c^2*x^3 at its boundary. The interior recurrence establishes strict noncapture and cubic limit 3c^2. Symbolic, rational and root checks were executed from the actual embedded verify.py path.

value.rationale: The key motivated question is whether a zero KKT multiplier permits finite identification under a newly introduced polynomial-time SOS-convexified higher-order Newton update, despite cubic local convergence. The theorem exactly classifies a natural minimal strongly convex, linearly constrained quartic family, quantifies the sharp positive-multiplier identification radius, and isolates tangential-to-normal coupling through an isotropic quartic regularizer. It is not just a general failure of strict complementarity, generic textbook projection fact, or arbitrary numerical slice; it gives an explicit algorithm-defined sharp frontier and asymptotic coefficient.
